subject: Business Models
title: WeWork: Growth at Any Cost
description: Learn WeWork: Growth at Any Cost in one minute.

hook.text: WeWork was valued at $47 billion in 2019. After its failed IPO, it was worth $8 billion. A 83% collapse.

buildup.text: WeWork signed long-term building leases and subleased desks on short-term contracts. It called this 'community.'

discovery.text: WeWork's model is simple: arbitrage between long and short lease terms. It's a real estate company, not a tech unicorn.

twist.text: CEO Adam Neumann cashed out $700 million before the collapse. The founder profited; the company nearly died.

climax.text: WeWork's 2023 bankruptcy proved that calling a real estate business 'tech' doesn't change the underlying economics.

punchline.text: $47B to bankruptcy. WeWork was real estate cosplaying as tech.

quiz.question: What was WeWork's actual business model beneath the 'tech' branding?
options: Lease arbitrage between long and short-term real estate contracts
